title: Thanksgiving break with kids in Spring Branch & Memorial (2026)
description: Free and cheap things to do with kids during SBISD's Thanksgiving break, Nov 23–27: storytimes, parks, free indoor play and kids-eat-free nights.
intro: Spring Branch ISD is out all week for Thanksgiving, Monday Nov 23 through Friday Nov 27. That's five days to fill, and the trick is to plan a few anchors before the week starts: a storytime, a long park morning, a free indoor play spot for a rainy day, and an easy dinner out.

Everything here is close to home in Spring Branch and Memorial, and most of it is free. Holiday weeks change library and restaurant schedules, so check each listing before you go, especially on Thursday.
The Saturday after the break, CityCentre's Holiday in the Plaza kicks off the holiday season (the date may still change). We'll add more events to this guide as they're announced.
tips: Libraries usually close or shorten hours around Thanksgiving, and storytimes can pause on holiday weeks. Check the branch calendar the week before.
Do outdoor plans early in the week and save the free indoor spots for whichever day it rains.
Frolic's Castle at Memorial City Mall requires socks, and weekday mornings are the quietest.
Ring Library's toddler storytime opens registration about two weeks ahead, so check the library calendar now for the break week.
Kids-eat-free nights change without notice, especially on holiday weeks. Call the restaurant before you go.

title: Free baby & toddler storytimes in Spring Branch & Memorial: the weekly schedule
description: Every week's free library storytimes for babies, toddlers and preschoolers near Spring Branch & Memorial, plus nature walks and cabin story hours.
intro: Storytime is the easiest outing there is with a baby or toddler: it's free, it's indoors, it's under an hour, and nobody minds if your kid wanders off mid-song. Spring Branch has two library systems close together, Harris County's Spring Branch Memorial Library on Corbindale and Houston Public Library's Ring and Hillendahl branches, so there's something most weekday mornings.

Here's the week at a glance: Wednesday is Baby Bouncers at Spring Branch Memorial or toddler storytime at Ring, and Thursday is Tiny Tykes for new walkers back at Spring Branch Memorial. Spring Branch Memorial also runs a preschool storytime with a craft for ages 3–6 (check the branch calendar for this month's day). Outdoorsy families can add a guided Tyke Hike at the Houston Arboretum (select Mondays: Nov 9 and 16, then Dec 7, 14 and 21) or a nature story in the log cabin at Edith L. Moore Nature Sanctuary.
Library schedules pause for holidays and change between seasons, so check each listing the week you go. We update this page whenever the libraries do.
tips: Arrive 15 minutes early. Popular storytimes hand out a limited number of free tickets, and they can run out.
Baby Bouncers and Tiny Tykes both run twice, at 10:15 and 11:15. If the first session is full or your kid naps late, aim for the second.
Ring Library's toddler storytime opens registration on the library calendar about two weeks ahead, so put a reminder in your phone.
Make a morning of it: Spring Branch Memorial Library has a playground next door, and Freed Park is a short drive from Ring Library.
It's fine to step out with a fussy baby and come back. Every storytime librarian has seen it all.

title: Holiday events & free Santa photos with kids near Spring Branch & Memorial (2026)
description: Free Santa photos, a Frozen movie night, a tree lighting and a kids' wreath workshop near Spring Branch & Memorial, Nov 28–Dec 5, 2026.
intro: The holiday season starts the Saturday after Thanksgiving break, and the best of it is close to home. CityCentre's Holiday in the Plaza on Sat Nov 28 has Santa, two of his reindeer and free professional photos. The next weekend, Memorial Park's Neighborhood Nights turns into a holiday movie night on Fri Dec 4, with Frozen on the lawn and photos with Santa, Anna and Elsa.

On Sat Dec 5 you can pick a crafty morning or a big night out: the Houston Arboretum's Homemade Holidays workshop has kids 5 and up making wreaths and ornaments, and downtown the Mayor's Deck the Hall tree lighting ends with fireworks.
Most of this is free, outdoors and weather-dependent, so check each listing the day before. We'll add more lights, Santa visits and holiday storytimes here as they're announced.
tips: Santa leaves Holiday in the Plaza at 4 pm. Go early, after lunch and before nap-time meltdowns, and bring something for the SPCA donation if you can.
Neighborhood Nights doesn't allow strollers or bikes. Bring a blanket, a carrier for the baby and layers: the lawn gets cold once the sun goes down.
Homemade Holidays has two sessions (11 am and 1 pm), each with its own tickets. Book early, and dress kids in clothes that can get sticky.
Toddler not a fan of Santa? Totally normal. A wave from across the plaza still counts as a holiday photo.
Outdoor holiday events can change for weather. Check the listing the morning of.

title: Rainy day with little kids in Spring Branch & Memorial: free indoor play
description: Free indoor play spots and storytimes for babies, toddlers and preschoolers near Spring Branch & Memorial, for rainy, cold or too-hot days.
intro: Houston weather cancels a lot of park mornings: a storm rolls in, a cold front blows through, or it's August. The good news is that Spring Branch and Memorial have free indoor options most days of the week, close to home.

The big one is Frolic's Castle at Memorial City Mall, a free three-story play castle for kids under 48 inches with a separate toddler area. For smaller kids there's the free indoor play area at Christ the King Presbyterian on Silber, open to the public some weekday mornings. And the three libraries nearby run free storytimes: Baby Bouncers on Wednesdays and Tiny Tykes on Thursdays at Spring Branch Memorial, plus toddler storytime at Ring on Wednesdays.

If you don't mind a short drive into town, two Heights-area spots are built for rainy days: The Bunny Hive's classes for babies through kindergarten, and Recess, a restaurant with two indoor playgrounds. We'll add more free indoor spots here as we find them.
tips: Frolic's Castle requires socks, so keep a spare pair in the diaper bag. Weekday mornings are the quietest; rainy Saturdays are the busiest.
Christ the King's play area hours vary by source. Call the church before you go.
Baby Bouncers and Tiny Tykes each run twice, at 10:15 and 11:15. If the first session is full, wait for the second.
On the first rainy day after a dry spell, everyone has the same idea. Go right at opening or after lunch.
Libraries are free indoor space even when there's no storytime: the picture-book corner and a stack of new books can fill an hour.
